Summary method for rrGDM models

Source: R/summary.R
summary.rrGDM.Rd

Summarises a fitted rrGDM object. The summary reports:

  • the model call and the (approximate marginal) log-likelihood;

  • for each predictor in the mean model, the effect size (Size, the modulus of its loadings across the latent dimensions) and a multivariate Wald test (see wald_test);

  • the intercept and slopes of the dispersion model (effects on \(\log(\tau)\), where \(\tau\) is the sample-level SD), with univariate Wald z-tests;

  • the standard deviation of additional random effects, if any;

  • the observation-level (pairwise) parameter of the response distribution, if the family has one (phi for beta and beta-binomial, SD for Gaussian)

  • the conditional stress and corR2 of the model.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'rrGDM'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted model of class rrGDM.

...

Currently unused.

Value

A list of class summary.rrGDM, with elements including call, loglik, df, aic, lambda (see wald_test), beta, tau0 (sample-level SD when all dispersion predictors are at their reference value), sigma_re, scale_par, stress_metric, stress_nonmetric and cor_r2.

Details

The log-likelihood is the approximate marginal log-likelihood obtained with the Laplace approximation, and df is the number of (non-mapped) fixed parameters estimated.

Two stress values are reported, both computed from the conditional latent coordinates (see stress): the metric stress on the dissimilarity (response) scale, and Kruskal's non-metric stress on the latent distances (link scale), which is the one comparable with NMDS software. The corR2 (see cor_r2) is the conditional squared correlation between observed and fitted dissimilarities. Both indicate how well the latent space captures the dissimilarities, but not the explanatory power of the predictors.

If the model was fitted without standard errors (se = FALSE), the Hessian at the optimum is not positive definite, or the covariance matrix of the estimates is missing, a warning is issued and only point estimates are reported.

If the stress or corR2 cannot be computed, a warning is given and the value is NA.

See also

wald_test, stress, cor_r2
